FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Ligue 1 strugglers Le Havre and Strasbourg’s new managers both seek their first wins in charge after suffering losses last week.

Match News and Current Form

Valérien Ismaël’s Le Havre reign began with a 3-1 defeat at fellow strugglers Troyes, leaving them at risk of becoming just the third side to claim fewer than three points from their opening 12 Ligue 1 games (D2, L9). The Sky and Navy have spent most of the campaign on the back foot, with no side conceding more than their 25 goals across the first 11 matchdays. Home form has deserted them too (D1, L5), and another defeat here would see Le Havre become the fourth team to lose at least six of their first seven home Ligue 1 games of a season.

Strasbourg are eight points better off than bottom side Le Havre, but start the round just two places above them after missing a late penalty in a 1-0 home defeat to Brest in Vítor Matos’s first game in charge. Le Racing are still in touch with the teams ahead of them despite losing six of their last seven Ligue 1 fixtures (W1), leaving them a whopping nine points worse off than the same stage of last season. Travel sickness has plagued Strasbourg this term, and they’re now at risk of losing five successive Ligue 1 away fixtures for the first time since November 2019.

Head-to-Head History

Just three of the previous 42 Ligue 1 H2Hs ended level (Le Havre: W20, L19), and none of the last six meetings hosted by Le Havre produced a draw either (W3, L3). Both H2Hs last season were won by the home side on the day.

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Four of Le Havre’s last five league fixtures produced over 3.5 goals.

Exactly one Le Havre player was booked in four of their last five home games.

Strasbourg are yet to score a Ligue 1 goal inside the opening 15 minutes this term.

Strasbourg have conceded 2+ goals in all six away league games this season (W1, L5).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

After netting against Troyes, Josh Maja has scored half of Le Havre’s ten league goals this term, with three of them arriving after the 70th minute. Strasbourg’s Dário Essugo has scored twice and picked up two yellow cards across his last six league appearances, remarkably opening the scoring in the 41st minute with both of those goals!

Enzo Koffi is suspended for Le Havre after being sent off against Troyes, while Rassoul Ndiaye is doubtful. Giovanni Reyna and Oso are among Strasbourg’s potential absentees.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

With Le Havre’s recent games producing plenty of goals and Strasbourg conceding regularly on the road this term, backing over 3.5 goals could be worth considering.

Author: John Pennington
